newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebels say they seized two army garrisons.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels say they seized two army garrisons.

text.p: Sudanese rebels said on Monday they captured two government army garrisons in southern Sudan, tightening the noose around the southern capital of Juba.
Yassir Arman, a spokesman for the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), dismissed as propaganda a commander of a militia allied to Khartoum saying five towns had been recaptured from the SPLA.
Arman said the SPLA captured the garrison town of Ayod on the Jonglei Canal 360 km (220 miles) north of Juba on Sunday and Tindilo garrison 120 km (75 miles) northwest of the southern capital.
He said a militia from the Nuer tribe fought alongside SPLA troops at Ayod and rebels seized two T-55 tanks and an anti-aircraft gun in fighting with an army column west of Tindilo.
"Those two battles expose the lies of the (Khartoum) regime and Riek Machar's group when they talk in the last two days about capturing Warab and Tali," Arman said in Eritrea's capital Asmara.
"We did not only capture Tali, but we moved and captured Tindilo and are putting more pressure on Juba and we have opened a new significant front by capturing Ayod in Upper Nile," he added.

Machar, commander of the Southern Sudan Defence Force, the unified force of several factions which signed a peace pact with the government in April, told a Khartoum newspaper at the weekend his forces had helped recapture five towns from rebels.
For 14 years the government has been fighting the SPLA, which wants greater autonomy or independence for the mostly Christian and animist south from the Moslem Arabised north.
